body:
The approved #669 rollout requires form review before merging `Sodium_Succinate_Dibasic` with `Sodium_Succinate`. Related: #738, #263 and #320.

The current identifiers agree on anhydrous disodium succinate: CAS 150-90-3, PubChem CID 9020 and CHEBI:63675. That alone does not settle the original generic record's supplied form. Its history includes supplier-derived CAS 6106-21-4 before a target-xref selection. The captured CultureBotHT input (SHA-256 `76b70a1836b25de431c4f5cc27c72bb6b06a223ce33911e93b7681d4fcdb28f9`, line 414) associates sodium succinate with Sigma S2378, 6106-21-4 and 270.14 g/mol. [Sigma S2378](https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/US/en/product/sial/s2378) is the hexahydrate; [Sigma 14160](https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/US/en/product/sial/14160) is a separate anhydrous product. Supplier evidence here is an inspected web extraction, not archived origin HTML. Existing recipe IDs derive from MIM and therefore do not independently settle the conflict.

For the approved bounded rollout, SUPPRESS `Sodium succinate` only on `MIM:Sodium_Succinate_Dibasic / skos:broadMatch / CHEBI:63675`, with a sidecar and unchanged source YAML. The alias is not established as chemically false, so it must not become REJECTED_LABEL. Preserve the explicit CHEBI:63686 hexahydrate control.

Options for the scientific decision:

- Trace the original product/form evidence and explicitly adopt an anhydrous naming convention for the generic source cohort, then merge through guarded writers with complete history, membership union and fresh review.
- If the source scope supports distinct forms, retain distinct identities and the §3 mapping pattern.

Recommendation: retain suppression and leave this issue open until that source scope or explicit evidence-backed convention is settled. No merge, replacement CAS or hydration state is inferred from the current target IDs. The bounded preflight and exact input hashes will accompany the consumer PR; this issue does not approve broader curation.
title: Resolve sodium succinate source hydration before merging dibasic and generic records

body:
Found by the #624 rebuild in #653.

`Potassium dibasic phosphate trihydrate` previously carried `CHEBI:131527` / CAS `7758-11-4`. The record behind that identifier is the **anhydrous** salt:

```
data/ingredients/mapped/K2hpo4.yaml
  identifier: CHEBI:131527
  preferred_term: K2HPO4
```

So a trihydrate was taking an anhydrous identity, which MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 refuses. The rebuild drops the match and the row is now `UNMAPPED` — correct, but it leaves the substance with no record at all, where the sodium-glutamate case at least has one to route to.

**Fix:** mint the trihydrate, per §3 — a form-specific ontology term if one exists, otherwise the registry pattern (`cas:` or `kgmicrobe.compound:`) with an asymmetric `skos:narrowMatch` to `CHEBI:131527` as the nearest parent, and both SSSOM rows per Rule B1.

Likely belongs to the #459 hydrate cohort (199 hydrate records / 173 formula-as-label records, overlapping by 95) rather than being worked alone; filing it separately so the specific name is not lost inside that cohort.

Not a blocker for #653.

body:
Found while measuring the #245 ruling (#735). Two `skos:broadMatch` parent rows point at a ChEBI term that is the substance itself, so Section 3 step 1 applies: `identifier` should be that term with `skos:exactMatch`, and the `cas:` own-identifier row retired per the decision procedure.

| record | identifier now | broadMatch object | why it is exact |
|---|---|---|---|
| `D-Raffinose pentahydrate` (`data/ingredients/mapped/D-Raffinose_Pentahydrate.yaml`) | `cas:17629-30-0` | `CHEBI:189430 Raffinose Pentahydrate`, formula `C18H32O16.5H2O` | same hydrate, same stoichiometry |
| `Sodium succinate dibasic` (`data/ingredients/mapped/Sodium_Succinate_Dibasic.yaml`) | `cas:150-90-3` | `CHEBI:63675 sodium succinate (anhydrous)`, formula `C4H4O4.2Na` | ChEBI's own xref for the term is `cas:150-90-3`; "dibasic" = disodium |

Both records are graded `NARROW_MATCH`. Changing them is an identity change, so it goes through the review bundle (#729–#731), not a hand edit; this issue is the record. Check the remaining 67 molecule-parent broadMatch rows for the same shape before applying (the check is: parent term's CAS xref equals the record's own CAS, or the parent's formula includes the hydrate stoichiometry the label states).

Related: #312, #245.
title: Two broadMatch rows anchor to a ChEBI term that denotes exactly the substance (step 1 says exactMatch)

body:
A root cause, found by an adversarial reviewer on #699 who noticed one instance and asked whether it was a pattern. It is.

4-Hydroxyphenylacetic acid has CAS RN `156-38-7`. Strip the hyphens and you get `156387` — and the record was once mapped to **`CHEBI:156387`, aspyrone**, an unrelated fungal metabolite. Swept across every mapped record's YAML (identifier, evidence, notes, curation_history):

| record | CAS RN | was mapped to | which is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3-Indolyl acetic acid | 87-51-4 | CHEBI:87514 | ethyl 2-hexenoate |
| 4-Hydroxyphenyl acetic acid | 156-38-7 | CHEBI:156387 | aspyrone |
| Phenyl acetic acid | 103-82-2 | CHEBI:103822 | LSM-15166 |
| Ethanol | 64-17-5 | CHEBI:64175 | a mannose tetrasaccharide |
| L-Cysteine HCl | 52-89-1 | CHEBI:52891 | QSY9 succinimidyl ester, a dye |
| DL-mevalonic acid | 150-97-0 | CHEBI:150970 | a sialylated oligosaccharide |
| Sodium succinate dibasic | 150-90-3 | CHEBI:150903 | a fucosyl trisaccharide |
| Na-pyruvate | 113-24-6 | CHEBI:113246 | a benzodioxinyl triazinone |
| Isovaleric acid / Na-L-lactate / Phenyl propionic acid | 503-74-2 / 867-56-1 / 501-52-0 | CHEBI:503742 / 867561 / 501520 | no such term |

**None is live.** Every one of the eleven mappings was later corrected, and a sweep finds **0** records today whose identifier equals a de-hyphenated CAS of their own.

**But the corrections left residue**, the same way the cadmium-nitrate names outlived the calcium-nitrate fix: the April `cbclaw_kg_microbe_sweep` enriched synonyms from the identifier it was about to reject, in the same run. For the eleven records:

- 3 had already had the residue retired in #699's first pass (found the long way round, by ChEBI label collision);
- **3 more still carried it live** — a sialyl-oligosaccharide's systematic name on DL-mevalonic acid, the QSY9 dye's on L-cysteine HCl, and three names including `Fuc(a1-3)[Glc(a1-4)]Gal` on disodium succinate. All five were published in the SSSOM `other` column. Retired in #699;
- 5 are clean.

## Still open

1. **Which importer did this, and is it still reachable?** I have the symptom and the history, not the code path. The mapped-to identifiers that *do not exist* (CHEBI:503742, 867561, 501520) say the value was never validated against ChEBI at write time, which narrows it.
2. **A guard.** The check is one line and has no legitimate false positive I can think of: a record's `CHEBI:` identifier digits must not equal any of its own CAS RNs with the hyphens removed. It passes today, which is the cheapest moment to pin it.
3. **The wider sweep this implies.** For every record whose history shows a corrected ontology id, are there live synonyms that ChEBI assigns to the *old* id and not the current one? #699 did this for ChEBI *labels* (34 hits, 13 unrelated compounds) and for these eleven by all names. It has not been done by all names across every remapped record.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01BP6MDZgidgzS79c75Ykhac
title: An importer read CAS numbers as ChEBI accessions: 11 records were mapped to CHEBI:<CAS with hyphens stripped>

Found reviewing #802. export_lists.py takes the first non-empty molecular formula per identifier in record order when computing ambiguity verdicts. After #799 the 'Sodium phosphate dibasic' tombstone shares CHEBI:34683 but still carries trisodium phosphate's formula (3Na.O4P), and Atrazin carries the erroneous CAS under CHEBI:15930. The survivor sorts first today, so verdicts are currently correct, but a record reorder would feed the wrong chemistry into the verdicts. Fix in #802: prefer MAPPED records' chemistry for each identifier.

---

title: Ambiguity formula lookup can take a tombstone's stale chemistry for its survivor's identifier

body:
## Problem

Four merge tombstones from the 2026-09-21 semantic review (#722) still carry their **old, rejected identity** as `identifier`, not their merge target:

| record | `identifier` (published) | merged into (per its `MERGED_INTO` event) |
|---|---|---|
| `Nano.yaml` (label `NaNO`) | `NCIT:C54713`, the *nano* unit prefix | `CHEBI:63005` (NaNO3) |
| `Atrazin.yaml` | `cas:1924-24-9` (an erroneous CAS) | `CHEBI:15930` (atrazine) |
| `Edta_Chelating_Agent.yaml` | `NCIT:C360` (chelating agents, a class) | `CHEBI:4735` (EDTA) |
| `Sodium_Phosphate_Dibasic.yaml` | `CHEBI:37583` (trisodium phosphate) | `CHEBI:34683` (Na2HPO4) |

`docs/LABEL_INDEX_CONTRACT.md` says: *"For a **merged** record the `identifier` already points at the merge target, so the row still resolves correctly and should be followed."* These four rows break that rule. A consumer that follows REJECTED rows, as the contract tells it to, resolves `NaNO` to the nano prefix and `Sodium phosphate dibasic` to trisodium phosphate. No live MAPPED row holds any of the four identifiers.

## How it surfaced

CultureMech's label-index reader refuses a pin with dangling tombstones. Once CultureBotAI/CultureMech#520 lets it read `AMBIGUOUS` rows, a preview refresh against MIM `7a65c4e9` fails with:

```
LabelIndexError: REJECTED merge tombstone identifier is not held by a live MAPPED row: CHEBI:37583, NCIT:C360, NCIT:C54713, cas:1924-24-9
```

So this now blocks CultureMech's MIM pin, which is 106 commits behind.

## Proposed fix

Point each tombstone's `identifier` at its merge target. Keep the original fields on the tombstone, as the merge events say they should be kept, and record the old identifier in the `curation_history` event. Every one of these record changes needs a `mapping_changes/` receipt through the review chain. Also add a MIM-side gate so a merge tombstone whose identifier no live record holds can't land (CultureMech already enforces this as a consumer).
title: Four 2026-09-21 merge tombstones keep their rejected identity instead of the merge target, breaking the label-index contract

body:
Found while grounding the CultureMech residual (#PR pending).

`HYDRATE_PATTERNS` in `src/mediaingredientmech/utils/chemical_normalizer.py` lists the
generic `\s*hydrate` **before** the specific `\s*heptahydrate` / `\s*dihydrate` /
`\s*monohydrate` / `\s*trihydrate`. Python applies them in order, so the generic pattern
matches the tail of the compound word first and leaves the multiplier stranded:

```
Sodium phosphate dibasic heptahydrate -> Sodium phosphate dibasic hepta
Magnesium sulfate heptahydrate        -> Magnesium sulfate hepta
Copper sulfate pentahydrate           -> Copper sulfate penta
Calcium chloride dihydrate            -> Calcium chloride di
Glucose monohydrate                   -> Glucose mono
Sodium acetate trihydrate             -> Sodium acetate tri
```

Every spelled-out hydrate in the corpus is affected; `pentahydrate` is not in the list at
all, so it can only ever hit the generic branch.

Two distinct problems:

1. **The stem is meaningless.** `Calcium chloride di` matches nothing in CHEBI, so the
   variant is dead weight in the search cascade rather than the anhydrous-parent variant
   it was meant to produce.
2. **The hydration state is silently dropped**, and hydration state is identity
   (MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md Section 3): `CaCl2` and `CaCl2 x 2 H2O` are 110.98 and 147.01
   g/mol. A caller that trusts `was_stripped=True` to mean "this is now the anhydrous
   parent" gets a corrupted string instead, with no way to tell the difference.

Suggested fix: order the alternatives longest-first (or use a single alternation
`(?:mono|di|tri|tetra|penta|hexa|hepta|octa|nona|deca)?hydrate`), and add a test that
asserts each multiplier round-trips to the bare compound name rather than to a stem.

Not fixed in the grounding PR: the normalizer is shared with the interactive curation
path, so changing it mid-batch would move results under work already reviewed.
title: strip_hydrate_notation truncates every spelled-out hydrate to a meaningless stem

body:
Found while adding synonym matching to CultureMech's divergence audit against
your published SSSOM (CultureBotAI/CultureMech#304).

## The defect

In `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv`, the row

```
subject_label : CaSO4 x 2 H2O
object_id     : CHEBI:32583  (calcium sulfate dihydrate)
```

carries **potassium phosphate aliases** in its `other` column:

```
other: (dibasic)|CaSO4|CaSO4 . 2H2O|CaSO4 x 2H2O|...|KH PO|KH2PO4|...|Potassium dihydrogen phosphate|...
```

`KH2PO4`, `KH PO` and `Potassium dihydrogen phosphate` are not aliases of calcium
sulfate dihydrate. They belong to the neighbouring `KH2PO4 → CHEBI:63036` row,
which is present and correct.

## Why it matters downstream

`Potassium dihydrogen phosphate` appears in the `other` column of **this row and
no other**, so a consumer that indexes aliases sees it as an unambiguous mapping
to `CHEBI:32583`. In CultureMech that would have told **233 ingredient rows** they
should be calcium sulfate dihydrate.

An ambiguity check does not help: a bad alias that occurs exactly once looks
exactly like a good one. We caught it only by eyeballing the newly-surfaced
disagreements before trusting them, and consequently left alias matching opt-in
rather than promoting it to our gate.

## Suggested fix

Remove the potassium-phosphate tokens from the `CaSO4 x 2 H2O` row's `other`.

Worth a sweep for the same shape, since whatever produced it may have merged
other adjacent rows: an alias whose element set is disjoint from its row's own
label is a cheap detector — `KH2PO4` shares no element with `CaSO4 x 2 H2O`
beyond O. CultureMech's `scripts/audit_name_term_elements.py` does the equivalent
check for groundings and could be adapted.

## Notes

- No action needed on CultureMech's side; we simply do not consume aliases by
  default.
- Happy to send the sweep results if that is useful.
title: CaSO4 x 2 H2O row carries KH2PO4 aliases, so consumers map potassium phosphate to calcium sulfate

body:
Surfaced by pointing the plausibility gate at the curator label (#261). These are **not** naming-convention noise — each is a record asserting a CHEBI id for an unrelated molecule, verified against live `sqlite:obo:chebi`.

| record | asserted id | what the id actually is | what the ingredient is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Casamino_Acids.yaml` | CHEBI:78020 | **heptacosanoate** (C27 fatty acid anion) | acid-hydrolysed casein digest — a peptide/amino-acid mixture |
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Na2s2o4.yaml` | CHEBI:61278 | **scutellarin** (a flavone glucuronide) | sodium dithionite, Na₂S₂O₄ — a reducing agent |
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Sodium_Succinate_Dibasic.yaml` | CHEBI:150903 | a trisaccharide-type glycoside (`(2S,3S,4R,5S,6S)-2-[…]oxane-3,4,5-triol`) | disodium succinate |
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Tomatidine_Hydrochloride.yaml` | CHEBI:93130 | `1-methyl-3-[…]-1,3,5-triazinane-2,4,6-trione` | tomatidine HCl, a steroidal alkaloid |

`Casamino acids → heptacosanoate` and `Na2S2O4 → scutellarin` are the starkest: nothing about either pair is chemically close, and both are common media ingredients, so the wrong id propagates into every export and downstream KG edge.

## Also worth a look (different failure class)

`Fructooligosaccharides (FOS)` → CHEBI:28645 **beta-D-fructofuranose**. Not an unrelated molecule, but a **granularity** error: a single monosaccharide standing in for an oligosaccharide mixture. Closer to the #237/#216 `DEFINED_MEDIUM` discussion than to the four above.

## Scope note

The gate reported 61 `IMPLAUSIBLE_LABEL` in total. **Most of the rest look like correct groundings** the lexical heuristic cannot see — `2-Furfuraldehyde` → *furfural*, `Irgasan` → *triclosan*, `Sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate` → *Mesna*, `Soy peptone` → *vegetable protein, hydrolyzed* (the very example the validator's own comment cites as a legitimate no-shared-word case). So the 61 is a **triage queue, not a defect count**, which is exactly why #261 holds this surface at `severity: warn` rather than flipping it to `error`.

These four, though, are confirmed and should be re-grounded.

Related: #261, #114.
title: Four verified wrong CHEBI groundings the no-op plausibility gate was hiding
